task_production_rates.name: Install floor protection at wainscot work zone
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Canvas drop cloth layout at wainscot base perimeter. Standard protection rate. Binary — same at all QTs.

task_production_rates.name: Mask wall above cap rail line
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr. Tape + 12-inch masking paper above cap rail for spray method. Standard masking rate. Binary. Spray only.

task_production_rates.name: Dust and clean all wainscot surfaces
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. Tack cloth or damp wipe all panels, rails, stiles. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Sand wainscot per substrate and state
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. SS_BARE: 150-220 grit full sand all surfaces. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: light scuff 150-180 only. Binary — prep sanding thoroughness does not vary by QT. Rate applies to flat_panel — apply wainscot_type modifier for raised_panel (1.25×) and beadboard (1.15×).

task_production_rates.name: Fill fastener holes and minor defects

QT5.notes: Fill all holes regardless of size, check with raking light

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled — higher QT fills more holes with greater precision. Rate based on typical fastener density in NC wainscot assembly.

task_production_rates.name: Sand filled areas smooth

QT4.notes: Sand flush, visual check each fill

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. 220 grit rigid sanding block (FFD §15.4.1). Rate reflects fill density — more fills at higher QT means more sanding.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk panel-to-frame internal joints
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Internal joint density ~1.4 LF/SF for flat_panel, higher for raised_panel. At ~60 LF/hr caulking rate, ~42 SF/hr for flat. Using 50 SF/hr as conservative estimate. Apply wainscot_type modifier for raised_panel. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk wainscot-to-wall junction
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Perimeter caulk at assembly-to-wall junction. ~0.5 LF/SF proportional to wainscot area. Continuous bead, tool smooth. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Detail work — shellac or oil-based sealer on all cut/routed edges and profiles. Wainscot has extensive routed profiles creating more edge area than simple trim. Conditional: substrate=mdf AND substrate_state=SS_BARE. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Prime wainscot panel assembly
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Full primer coat on all wainscot surfaces. Rate covers typical brush prime on panel faces and frame members. Spray prime may be faster but rate captures average. Binary — primer application quality not tiered. Conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE.

task_production_rates.name: Light sand primer for finish coat adhesion
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. 220 grit light sand entire primed surface. Quick pass for tooth. Tack cloth after. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on wainscot
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat_panel at baseline. Spray technique: field panels first (broad passes), then frame detail (fine tip). Rate includes detail time at frame profiles. Apply wainscot_type modifier: raised_panel ÷1.25, beadboard ÷1.15. Binary — application quality not tiered. Derived from brief estimate 150-200 SF/hr and Millwork Doctrine §7.1.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on wainscot
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat_panel at baseline. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). Roll and Tip on flat panels (FFD §15.6). Apply wainscot_type modifier: raised_panel ÷1.25, beadboard ÷1.15. Binary — application quality not tiered. Derived from brief estimate 60-80 SF/hr and Millwork Doctrine §7.1 trim rates adapted for SF.

task_production_rates.name: Clean work area between coats
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. Remove dust/debris from floor protection and work area. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect previous coat

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6ft — obvious defects only

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3ft — all visible defects marked

QT5.notes: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance. Check panel-to-frame junctions for holidays.

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Wainscot inspection at arm's length (QT5) is detail-intensive due to panel joints and profiles.

task_production_rates.name: Sand between coats

QT5.notes: Thorough 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern. Flexible sponge for beadboard grooves and raised panel profiles.

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Rigid sanding block mandatory on flat panels (FFD §15.4.1). Apply wainscot_type modifier for profile complexity.

task_production_rates.name: Patch and repair marked defects
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled — scope of repair increases with tier.

task_production_rates.name: Spot coat patched areas
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled. Touch-up patched areas before next full coat.

task_production_rates.name: Tack cloth all wainscot surfaces
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Per interstage cycle. Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Final quality inspection

QT4.notes: Systematic review at 3ft of all surfaces

QT5.notes: Critical lighted inspection at arm's length. Check junctions, sheen uniformity, groove definition.

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Key checkpoints: panel-to-frame holidays, brush marks on flat panels, groove definition on beadboard, caulk lines, sheen uniformity.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-up defects from final inspection
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. qt_scaled. Correct remaining defects. Feather touch-ups into surrounding finish.

task_production_rates.name: Remove wall masking
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr. Score tape edge, pull at 45-degree angle. Spray method only. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Remove floor protection
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Fold canvas drop cloths inward to contain debris. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum work area
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Vacuum floor after protection removal. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Clean tools and equipment
task_production_rates.notes: Per session. Clean brushes, spray equipment, dispose of consumables. Water cleanup for waterborne; solvent for shellac residue. Binary.

wainscot_panel.rationale: Standard wainscot is 32-42 inches tall. All work performed standing or kneeling. No access equipment needed. Always H1.

quality_tier_modifiers.applies_to: qt_scaled tasks only (inspection, sanding, fill, repair)
quality_tier_modifiers.does_not_apply_to: application tasks (brush/spray finish, prime) — application quality is NOT tiered

wainscot_type_modifier.application_rule: Modifiers increase TIME, not rate. effective_rate = base_rate ÷ modifier. Apply to ALL qt_scaled tasks and to application tasks (spray_finish, brush_finish, prime_faces, caulk_joints, seal_mdf_edges, sand_prep).
wainscot_type_modifier.notes: flat_panel=baseline (standard flat panels with simple frame), raised_panel=complex 3D profile with detail edges (1.25× time), beadboard=uniform vertical grooves requiring additional attention (1.15× time). Beadboard modifier (1.15×) is interpolated — doctrine has standard 1.0× and complex 1.25× but beadboard falls between.

round_configurations.notes: May also include MOD_WNSC_PRIME if SS_BARE (4 total coats, 3 interstages).

estimation_notes.sf_based: All wainscot tasks use SF as the primary UOM. SF from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WAINSCOTING — no conversion needed.
estimation_notes.wainscot_type_impact: Raised panel adds ~25% time due to 3D profile detail. Beadboard adds ~15% due to groove attention. Flat panel is baseline. Apply as TIME modifier (÷ modifier value).
estimation_notes.spray_vs_brush: Spray is ~2.5× faster than brush on flat panels (175 vs 70 SF/hr). Gap narrows for raised_panel and beadboard where detail work is required regardless of method.
estimation_notes.no_dry_times: Per RC-004: no dry times specified. Refer to manufacturer PDS.
estimation_notes.caulk_rate_basis: Internal caulk rate (50 SF/hr) based on estimated ~1.4 LF internal joints per SF at ~60 LF/hr caulking throughput. Wall junction rate (120 SF/hr) based on ~0.5 LF perimeter per SF.

assumptions.value: 175 SF/hr for flat_panel wainscot spray finish
assumptions.source: Brief Section 13 — estimated 150-200 SF/hr, midpoint used
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides wainscot-specific SF spray rates. Derived from Millwork Doctrine §7.1 trim rates adapted for panel SF.

assumptions.value: 70 SF/hr for flat_panel wainscot brush finish
assumptions.source: Brief Section 13 — estimated 60-80 SF/hr, midpoint used
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides wainscot-specific SF brush rates. Derived from Millwork Doctrine §7.1 trim brush rate of 80 LF/hr.

assumptions.source: Brief Section 13 — interpolated between standard (1.0×) and complex (1.25×)
assumptions.note: Millwork Doctrine §7.2 has standard and complex categories but no explicit beadboard modifier. 1.15× is reasonable interpolation.

assumptions.value: ~1.4 LF of internal joints per SF of flat_panel wainscot
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical 4'×3' wainscot section geometry
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines joint density. Used to derive SF/hr caulk rate from LF/hr caulking throughput.
